Dear #MAGA, we need to address the history how the US was built because I think there’s an issue with your understanding of history.

Over the past 250 years, America was built by a mix of willing immigrants, enslaved people, displaced Indigenous communities, and exploited labour, all woven into a complex, often painful history.

Here’s a breakdown of who helped build America and where they came from:

🇺🇸 1. Indigenous Peoples (Pre-1776 – Present)
Where from: Already here.
Contribution: The original stewards of the land. They taught early settlers how to farm, hunt, and survive. But they were violently displaced, massacred, and driven off their lands to make way for expansion.

⚒️ 2. Enslaved Africans (1600s–1865)
Where from: West and Central Africa, brought forcibly through the transatlantic slave trade.
Contribution: The backbone of early American agriculture, especially cotton, tobacco, sugar, and rice. They didn’t “immigrate.” They were trafficked. America's economic rise is directly tied to slavery.

🌍 3. Immigrants from Europe (1700s–1900s)
British, Irish, Germans, Italians, Scandinavians, Eastern Europeans
Why they came: Escape poverty, religious persecution, famine, or political unrest.
What they did: Built infrastructure, canals, railroads, bridges, mines. Worked in factories and textile mills. Established cities, schools, businesses.

🛤️ 4. Chinese Immigrants (mid-1800s)
Where from: Southern China
What they did: Instrumental in building the western portion of the Transcontinental Railroad. Faced brutal discrimination and violence, culminating in the Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882.

🧱 5. Mexican & Central American Labourers (1900s–Present)
Where from: Mexico, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras
What they did: Migrant farmworkers, meatpacking, construction, domestic work. Many undocumented, yet critical to the U.S. economy.

🪖 6. Black Americans (Post-Slavery to Civil Rights Era and Beyond)
Where from: Descendants of enslaved people, living primarily in the South initially.
What they did: Fought for rights they were denied. Built Black Wall Streets, served in every war, and contributed across industry, culture, academia, and activism, all while being systemically oppressed.

🧬 7. Scientists, Entrepreneurs, Innovators (1900s–Present)
Where from: All over the world. Notably from Europe (Jewish refugees during WWII), India, China, Russia, Iran, and beyond.
What they did: Shaped Silicon Valley, the space race, biotech, and modern American innovation.

🌐 8. Modern Global Immigrants (1965–Present)
Post-1965 Immigration Act opened doors to non-Europeans.
Came from: India, Philippines, Nigeria, Vietnam, Korea, Haiti, the Middle East, and more.
Contributions: Medicine, tech, engineering, academia, small business, and service industries.

❗ Don’t Forget:
Women of all backgrounds were invisible in many records but crucial in every generation, as workers, organisers, educators, and caregivers.

LGBTQ+ communities played pivotal roles in activism, arts, tech, and culture.

Refugees and asylum seekers often brought incredible resilience and drive.

TL;DR Summary:
America wasn’t built by one group or one story.
 It was forged in contradiction: by free and unfree people, by immigrants and Indigenous resistance, by capitalists and abolitionists, by dreamers and those who had no choice.

Everyone contributed, but not everyone was rewarded equally.

Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 45 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Enhanced Southwest Monsoon (Habagat)
Issued at: 5:00 AM, 23 July 2025(Wednesday)

ORANGE WARNING LEVEL: Zambales and Bataan.
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING is still THREATENING.

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Laguna, Rizal, Batangas, Cavite, Metro Manila, Pampanga(Floridablanca, Lubao, Sasmuan, Macabebe, Mabalacat, Porac, Angeles, Masantol) and Tarlac(Capas, Bamban, San Jose, Mayantoc, San Clemente, Camiling, Santa Ignacia).
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, expect light to moderate with occasional heavy rains over Nueva Ecija within the next 3 hours.
Light to moderate with occasional heavy rains affecting Bulacan, Quezon, Pampanga(Apalit, Arayat, Bacolor, Candaba, San Fernando, Magalang, Mexico, Minalin, San Luis, San Simon, Santa Ana, Santo Tomas, Guagua, Santa Rita) and Tarlac(Concepcion, Anao, Tarlac City, Gerona, La Paz, Paniqui, Pura, Ramos, San Manuel, Victoria, Moncada) which may persist within 3 hours.

The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 8:00 AM today.
For more information and queries, please call telephone numbers 8927-1335 and 8927-2877 or log on to https://t.co/59mTpZJq1n.
